column1: # Nine Commits, post 3 — what each run actually read.
# One row per run for rows 22-42 of runs.tsv, derived from their traces by
# walking every search_files result. Generated, not typed:
# tools/corpus-reach.ts is committed, so the derivation can be read and
# re-run even though these 21 raw traces are not in the tree — they are about
# a megabyte of repeated listings of this same repository. One of them IS
# committed, in full and normalised like any other: trace2-corpus-hit.json is
# tally-06, the row where post 2's answer sentence and the ground truth arrive
# in the same tool result. It goes through the same leak gate as every other
# trace here; `npm run validate` scans it.
# post_files_matched  every file under site/src/content/posts/ that appeared in
#                     that run's search results — the published posts 1 and 2.
# saw_post2_answer_line  the run's results included 02-hands/index.mdx line 102,
#                     which states both graded facts in one sentence.
# saw_cli_usage_line  the run's results included the usage example in
#                     agent/src/cli.ts, which also states both facts.
# saw_config_ts_line  the run's results included agent/src/config.ts line 1,
# answer_names_a_post  whether the final answer referred to a post, a README, a
#                     .mdx file or DECISIONS.md rather than to the source. The
#                     answer itself is the last column, so this is checkable
#                     rather than a judgement you have to take on trust.
